verdict.rationale: Fellow lets users generate multiple named API keys, recommending one per application. It distinguishes User, Workspace and Super Admin keys. For agent access through MCP, admins decide which tools members' AI assistants can use, connections only see data the user already has, and owners can revoke connections and see last-used timestamps. However, nothing shows that an individual API key can be limited to specific scopes, endpoints or read-only access; user keys simply inherit the user's full permissions. Missing for 10: per-key permission scopes (e.g. read-only or resource-limited keys), per-credential rather than workspace-wide MCP tool restrictions, key expiry or rotation controls, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
